audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with their own whys[] text and with both the packet and the mirror: Level 3 read Jax while whys[2] calls it skill-decided, Levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] says his steroids beat your burst, First item read Skill while whys[5] says he still out-damages you, and 2+ items read Jax while whys[6] says you out-scale him there.
audit.why: The packet agrees with the prose on six of seven rows, and the audited mirror agrees that two items is where the lane flips to you. 48.99% over 5809 games is a lane you survive rather than win early.
audit.corrected: Jax, Jax, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Yone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ultimate is called 'Grandmaster's Might' in whys[4] and spikes[1]; no cooldowns appear anywhere.
audit.why: The real name is Grandmaster-at-Arms, 110/100/90s, and it is a passive third-strike plus an active that raises his armour and MR. Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 collapsing to 9s — the single number this lane is played around. Empower is 7s at rank 1 down to 3s. Leap Strike is 8s to 6s. Your Soul Unbound falls 22s to 10s.
audit.corrected: Names and numbers written into whys[4], spikes[0], spikes[1] and the interaction rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described as 'dodges autos + stuns' with no statement of what it does NOT stop, and Fate Sealed is described as setting up team knockups.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit that Counter Strike dodges incoming ATTACKS — Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave and Fate Sealed are abilities and still land through it, which changes the trade from 'wait it out doing nothing' to 'stop auto-attacking and keep casting'. Empower is an auto-attack reset, so his burst is telegraphed by the wind-up rather than by a visible cast. Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls; the knockup here is your own Mortal Steel at two stacks.
audit.corrected: Keep casting through Counter Strike and stop auto-attacking; its 17 seconds at rank 1 is your commit window. Fate Sealed pulls, it does not knock up.

audit.why: report[8].t carries no Grievous Wounds line here — correct, since nothing in Jax's kit heals. The mirror had to strip that advice from four places on its own page; this side is already clean.

notes: The ultimate was named 'Grandmaster's Might' in two places; the real name is Grandmaster-at-Arms. The most useful addition is the Counter Strike distinction: Riot's text says it dodges incoming ATTACKS, so your abilities still connect — the correct play inside it is to stop auto-attacking and keep casting, not to stand still doing nothing. Four chart rows flipped in matched pairs; the resulting chart agrees with the packet, with this page's whys[] and with the mirror at two items. Difficulty moved from a self-contradictory EVEN/8.5/red to TRICKY 7.5/10 on a 48.99% win rate.
